feat(compliance): JSON/HTML compliance-matrix endpoint per threat model
pulls.body:
## Why this matters (plain language)

Compliance reviewers (SSPP authors, FedRAMP assessors, security engineers) need to see, for a given threat model, which NIST-800-53 controls are covered by which countermeasures — and which controls have nothing pointing at them. Today Precogly stores all the underlying data (`StandardRequirement`, `InstanceCountermeasureStandard`, `CountermeasureThreatLink`, plus `ctrl_id` in threat metadata), but there's no single endpoint that puts it together into a per-threat-model matrix.

This PR adds a read-only endpoint that returns exactly that: one row per control, with the countermeasures satisfying it, the threats mapped to it, and provenance for each mapping. There's a JSON API for programmatic use and an HTML variant for browser preview.

## Value

- Turns Precogly into a viable "single pane of glass" for SSPP-style compliance-matrix reviews without leaving the tool.
- No schema change — pure read-side. Safe to add on top of any tenant's existing data.
- Multi-tenancy is honored via `ThreatModel.visible_to`, so a user hitting a threat model outside their scope gets 404, not a data leak.

## What this changes

- New endpoints:
  - `GET /api/threat-models/<tm_id>/compliance-matrix/?framework=<name>` — JSON, default framework `NIST 800-53 Rev 5`.
  - `GET /api/threat-models/<tm_id>/compliance-matrix.html` — HTML render of the same payload.
- Row schema: one row per `StandardRequirement`, grouped by control family (AC, AU, CM, ...), each row projects countermeasures + threats with sufficiency and provenance.
- Threat-side `ctrl_id` fallback: reads `ComponentInstanceThreat.format_metadata['cyclonedx']['ctrl_id']` (and the `DataFlowInstanceThreat` equivalent), so threats generated by the CycloneDX SSPP flow that carry a control id directly still surface — interim until a first-class `ThreatStandard` model lands.
- `include_empty` query flag to show controls with no mapping (drives the "gap" view in SSPP review).
- Golden JSON snapshot fixture committed as `tests/fixtures/matrix_snapshot.json` to pin the payload contract.

## Split note

The fork branch this came from (`feat/compliance-matrix-view`, identical to `feat/cloudgov-keycloak-sso`) also carried cloud.gov / Keycloak SSO and podman-compose changes. Those are unrelated and are being landed separately (podman is PR #551). This PR isolates just the compliance-matrix commits onto current `main`. The `uv.lock` entries the cherry-pick pulled in for the SSO deps were dropped in a follow-up commit — this PR adds no new Python dependencies.

## Independence

- No schema change; no migration.
- Files touched are disjoint from PRs #559 (threats/cyclonedx), #560 (packs/systems/frontend icon), and #551 (docker-compose overlay). Safe to merge in any order relative to those.

## Testing

- `ruff check` clean on touched files.
- `apps/compliance` suite (14 tests) passes; full backend suite (333 tests) passes with no regressions.
- `makemigrations --check --dry-run`: no changes.

pulls.title: feat(packs): pack-level icon via safe SVG-file loading
pulls.body: ## Why this matters (plain language) Precogly's DFD nodes render a technology icon next to the node label — for example, an S3 bucket shows an S3 logo. Today only individual components in a pack can declare an icon; the pack itself can't. That means threat libraries and template packs (which have a strong brand identity — "AWS", "Azure", "OWASP") show a generic square in the UI, and components without their own icon have no visual context for which pack they came from. This PR gives packs a first-class icon field and lets components without their own icon fall back to their pack's icon. Everything renders through the existing safe base64-`` pipeline introduced by the #516 XSS fix — no new rendering path and no new npm dependency. ## Value - Restores brand context in the DFD editor (AWS pack components look like AWS things even if a specific service has no bespoke icon yet). - Same XSS-safety guarantee as the existing per-component icon mechanism — pack-supplied SVGs are never injected as raw HTML. - No new frontend dependency. No new backend dependency. Migration is a single additive `TextField`. ## Context on the earlier attempt An earlier branch (`feature/icon-library-mvp`) tried to add pack icons by introducing `@thesvg/react`, a JSON icon config (slug / variant / className / style), and raw-SVG-component rendering. It was written before #516 landed. Merging it as-is would (a) re-introduce a raw-markup icon rendering path that #516 deliberately removed, and (b) run two incompatible icon pipelines side-by-side. This PR keeps the value (pack + component-level fallback) by extending the *existing, already-reviewed* mechanism one level up, from component to pack. Not carried over: per-component icon JSONField overrides, vendor-brand-logo resolution via `@thesvg/react`, and the dual vendor+service icon render. Re-adding equivalents needs a fresh design that keeps the base64-`` constraint. Happy to scope that as a follow-up. ## What this changes **Backend** - `LibraryPack.icon_svg` (`TextField`, same shape as `ComponentLibrary.icon_svg`), migration `packs/0003_librarypack_icon_svg`. - Pack importer reads an optional `pack.yaml` `icon: ` (relative to the pack dir), mirroring the existing per-component `icon: ` convention in `components.yaml`. Missing files warn; nothing throws. - `LibraryPackListSerializer` / `LibraryPackDetailSerializer` expose `icon_svg` (viewset is `ReadOnlyModelViewSet`, so no write path is added). - `ComponentLibrarySerializer` gains `source_pack_icon_svg` so a component without its own icon can fall back to its pack's icon. **Frontend** - `ComponentLibraryItem.sourcePackIconSvg`; `transformToTechnology` and `ComponentPanel` fall back to it. - Everything still flows through the existing `SvgIcon` component (base64 data-URI ``, never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`). **Docs** - `creating-library-packs.md` documents the `pack.yaml` `icon:` key and explains why it's safe. ## Independence - Migration `packs/0003_librarypack_icon_svg` is additive and independent. - Files touched are disjoint from PRs #559 (threats/cyclonedx), #561 (compliance app), and #551 (docker-compose overlay). Safe to merge in any order relative to those. ## Testing - Backend: `ruff check` clean; new `apps/packs/test_pack_icon_svg.py` (4 tests) + full `apps/packs`, `apps/systems`, and template-pack-visibility suite (51 total) pass; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports no changes. - Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on touched files.

pulls.title: feat(cyclonedx): complete satisfies/externalReferences import + POA&M tracking
pulls.body:
## Why this matters (plain language)

Precogly can already import CycloneDX Threat-Model BOMs (TM-BOMs), but the importer today drops several fields that FedRAMP / SSPP-style workflows depend on: which NIST control a countermeasure claims to satisfy, the evidence URL for each control, and Plan-of-Action-and-Milestones (POA&M) tracking (`poam:id`, scheduled completion date, whether a control is overdue). Users generating a TM-BOM from a compliance tool and importing it into Precogly currently lose that context and have to re-enter it by hand.

This PR closes those gaps so a TM-BOM round-trips through Precogly with its compliance and POA&M metadata intact.

## Value

- Enables using Precogly as the visualization/threat-analysis layer for teams whose source of truth is a CycloneDX TM-BOM (GSA SSPP flow, FedRAMP submissions, etc.) without losing control-mapping fidelity.
- Adds first-class POA&M fields on `InstanceCountermeasure`, so overdue controls surface in the API without a custom join.

## What this changes

- **POA&M fields on `InstanceCountermeasure`**: `poam_id`, `scheduled_completion`, and a `source` enum (`manual` / `vault_import` / `pentest`), plus a `days_overdue` property that ignores `IMPLEMENTED` / `VERIFIED` controls. The CycloneDX importer parses `poam:id` and `poam:scheduled-completion` control properties.
- **`satisfies[]` import**: imports `definitions[].requirements`, creates `InstanceCountermeasureStandard` rows for each control's `satisfies[]`, resolving `StandardRequirement` FK when the framework is installed. When the framework isn't installed, we keep section_code / framework_name / description snapshots so the mapping still displays and round-trips on export. Dangling references warn and skip. Multiple unresolved mappings per control are all preserved (previously only the last survived).
- **`externalReferences` import**: a control externalReference typed `evidence` populates `InstanceCountermeasure.evidence_url`.
- **`crosses_trust_zone`**: `DataFlow` imported from `blueprint.flows` sets `crosses_trust_zone` when source and destination sit in different trust zones.
- Refactors requirement-snapshot construction into a single helper.

Closes tracking issues in GSA-TTS/TTSE-petrified-forest-sspp#31.

## Independence

- Migration `threats/0015_poam_fields` is additive and independent (numbered above current `main`'s `threats/0014`).
- Files touched are disjoint from PRs #560 (packs/systems/frontend icon), #561 (compliance app), and #551 (docker-compose overlay). Safe to merge in any order relative to those.

## Testing

- `backend/apps/threats/tests/test_poam_fields.py` — POA&M model fields, `days_overdue`, API filters.
- `backend/apps/threat_models/tests/test_cdx_poam_import.py` — CycloneDX `poam:*` property parsing on import.
- `backend/apps/threat_models/tests/test_cdx_import_audit.py` — resolved/unresolved/dangling satisfies, evidence-url mapping, zone-crossing flags, satisfies round-trip.
- Full backend suite: `345 passed` (no regressions).
- `manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run`: no missing migrations.
- `ruff check`: clean.

## Draft note

Marked draft — awaiting a first pass of upstream review on the `satisfies[]` snapshot-vs-resolved contract (do we prefer snapshot-only when the framework isn't installed, or block the import?). Happy to switch behavior if reviewers want stricter semantics.

feat(dfd-editor): merge table cells and STRIDE worksheet template
pulls.body:
Three things that belong together: merging cells, the worksheet that needed
merging, and a context-menu bug the cell selection in #553 shipped with.

Select a range and merge it, so a table can carry a header spanning the columns
under it. That is what a STRIDE-per-interaction worksheet needs (#520): a
component name over its Mitigations/Weaknesses pair, which is the layout Vikram
posted and the reason this exists. That worksheet now ships as a template pack
rather than living only in my checkout.

Screenshot of the rebuilt worksheet is at `frontend/tmp/stride-merged.png` in my
checkout if you want it dropped in here; I can't attach images from the CLI.

## Behaviour, and where it comes from

Checked against the tools on 2026-09-16 rather than guessed.

**Interaction is Miro's** — select cells, *Merge cells* on the context menu, and
they can be unmerged at any time.

**Content is Excel's rule** — the anchor keeps its text, the rest are emptied.
[Microsoft](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/merge-and-unmerge-cells-in-excel):
"the contents of only one cell (the upper-left cell…) appear in the merged cell.
The contents of the other cells that you merge are deleted." Sheets is the same.

**No confirmation, unlike both of them.** They warn because in Excel and Sheets
the discarded text is gone for good — Microsoft's doc is explicit that unmerge
does not bring it back. Undo restores it here, and the table already discards
cells without asking when a row or column is removed, with the panel saying so:
*"Removing a column or row discards its cells. Undo restores them."*

**An insert or delete through a merge unmerges it.** Neither spreadsheet does
anything better. Excel expands the selection to the merge's full extent, so
inserting one row inside a ten-row merge inserts
[ten](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5033930/insert-columns-rows-where-there-are-merged-cells);
Sheets often refuses the insert outright. In both, the documented workaround is
unmerge → edit → re-merge, which is what this does for you. Notion does not
support merging at all.

## Data model

Spans live on the anchor as `colSpan`/`rowSpan`, absent meaning one, so a diagram
saved before merging existed is already correct. The cells a merge swallows stay
in the array, keeping the grid rectangular so every index into it still means
what it did. Which cells are covered is **derived** from the anchors, not
flagged — a flag and the span it mirrors are two things that can disagree.

This also answers the open question in #520. A span composes with a later field
pointing at a child node, so a cell that both spans and contains is just an
anchor carrying both. The two features do not need settling together.

## The worksheet

`libraries/packs/worksheets/stride-worksheets`, one template: **STRIDE per
Interaction**. Two elements and the flow between them, a row per STRIDE
category, a Mitigations/Weaknesses pair per element.

**Greyed cells are semantic, not styling** — the categories that do not apply to
that element type, from Vikram's heuristic in #520 (external entity: T, I, D, E;
data store: S, E; data flow: S, R, E; process: none). Grey therefore means "not
applicable" throughout the worksheet, which is why the header rows are yellow: a
grey header would read as a struck-out row.

**`pack_type: template`, not `full`.** It carries no components, threats or
countermeasures. A worksheet is a method rather than a technology domain, so it
has nothing to contribute to the suggestion engine and nothing to join against a
taxonomy — it is complete as it stands, not an unfinished pack.

## Template packs are offered without being connected

`DFDTemplatesLibraryViewSet.get_queryset` gated every template on its source
pack being connected to the threat model, so the `component_ref`s in it resolve;
an AWS template inserted without the AWS pack yields components pointing at
nothing. A template pack ships no components, so a connection has nothing to
supply, and gating it would make a facilitator connect a STRIDE worksheet to
their model as though it described their stack. Those packs are now exempt.

I traced the path from pack YAML to canvas and called it a passthrough before
finding this, which was wrong — the gate sits in a queryset upstream of every
hop I looked at. It only turned up by inserting the template against a running
stack.

## Bugs fixed here

**Merged cells were not clickable through the middle.** Divider drag strips span
the whole table, so the strip for the boundary between two merged rows lay across
the centre of the merged cell — exactly where a pointer lands — and started a row
resize instead. Dividers are now emitted in runs that skip any boundary a merge
crosses. Found by a test timing out on `cursor-row-resize … intercepts pointer
events`; it would have shipped otherwise.

**Arrow keys walked into merged blocks.** Stepping right from a two-wide merge
landed on a covered cell, which renders nothing, so the selection appeared to
vanish. The covered map carries each cell's anchor, and `moveFocus` steps out of
the whole block rather than one cell at a time.

**The context menu would not close over a selected table** — this one shipped in
#553. A selected table swallowed the pointerdown on its cells, so an open menu
stayed open until a click landed outside the table; an unselected one was fine,
since only a selected table takes the pointer at all. React's `stopPropagation`
stops the native event at the root container, and Radix dismisses layers from a
`pointerdown` listener on `document` above it. Nothing needed the stop: `nodrag`
is what keeps a press from dragging the node, and no ancestor of a cell handles
`pointerdown` (@xyflow/react 12.10.0 — its only React-level one is on `Handle`, a
descendant, and the pane's is capture-phase).

## Verification

- `npx playwright test` — 36 passed, including a regression test for the menu
  that fails on the previous commit (`toBeHidden` → received visible).
- `manage.py test apps.diagrams.tests.test_template_pack_visibility` — 2 passed,
  covering both halves: the template pack is offered unconnected, and every other
  pack is still gated.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` clean on every file touched.
- Inserted the worksheet from the template browser against a running stack, with
  the pack imported and deliberately not connected to any threat model — the
  state a real user is in.

## Look hardest at

- `expandRangeOverMerges`. Merging a range that cuts an existing merge would
  leave two anchors claiming one cell, which nothing downstream can render. It
  grows the range to swallow whole merges, iterated to a fixed point because
  widening to absorb one can bring the edge against another.
- The queryset relaxation. Widening it further would break technology templates
  quietly, which is why the second test matters more than the first.
- The divider runs, which are the least obvious part of the diff and exist only
  because of the click-stealing bug above.

## Left out

- Merging is not offered across a selection that is already partly merged in a
  way the expansion cannot resolve; it simply widens instead. No case found where
  that is wrong, but it is the area I would fuzz first.
- The guest editor gets no templates, deliberately, so the worksheet is not
  reachable there.
- Reassigning a worksheet column group to a different element type means
  re-greying its column pair by hand. The greys are keyed to the three types the
  template ships with.

pulls.title: feat(dfd-editor): select and fill table cells
pulls.body:
Canvas tables could only carry text. This adds a cell selection and a colour
fill on top of it, so a row can be marked as the risky one — the first thing
anyone reaches for in a threat model.

Builds on the table node from #<!-- canvas-table-node -->, already on `main`.

## What's here

Six commits, each self-contained:

| commit | |
|---|---|
| `chore(ui)` | context menu submenu primitives, matching shadcn's canonical output |
| `fix(dfd-editor)` | a pre-existing focus bug, see below |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | select cells — click, drag, row/column grips |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | fill them with a colour |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | arrow keys move the selection, shift-arrow extends it |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | the picker shows what the selection already carries |

## Decisions, and what was rejected

**Two-stage drag.** An unselected table drags from anywhere in its body like
every other node; once selected, a press on a cell belongs to the table and the
table moves from its grips. The alternative was a dedicated always-visible drag
border, which costs an affordance on every table and breaks "grab the middle and
move it" outright. This is the Miro rule. It is the change most likely to feel
wrong in the hand, so it is the thing to try first.

`nodrag` on the cells is what enforces it — not the `stopPropagation` in the
hook. React Flow drags from a native listener on the node wrapper, which has
already run by the time a React handler on a descendant fires. The first version
used `stopPropagation` alone and the table moved along with the selection drag.

**Fill is stored per cell**, not per row or column. So a row inserted into a
filled column arrives unfilled, which is visible. The alternative was resolving
cell over column over row on every render and giving "clear this cell" two
meanings.

**The eight colours** are the intersection of Notion's, Google Sheets' and
Airtable's palettes, checked 2026-09-16. Brown is Notion-only; cyan and teal are
absent from Notion; these eight are in all three. Five of the values are already
the sticky note tints, so a yellow cell matches a yellow sticky note beside it —
`TABLE_FILL_COLORS` records that the two sets have to move together, and that
they are frozen Tailwind v3 values while the project runs v4.

**Gray is slate-200, not slate-100.** The header row paints itself slate-100, so
a slate-100 gray would be invisible on row 0 and would read as a second header
row anywhere else.

**No shift-click to extend**, though every spreadsheet has one. Shift is React
Flow's `selectionKeyCode` and a pointerdown under it never reaches the cell;
measured on the guest canvas, Alt and Meta get through and Shift does not.
Keydowns are untouched, which is why shift-*arrow* works. Restoring shift-click
means `selectionKeyCode={null}` on the ReactFlow in `DFDEditor` and
`GuestDFDEditor`, whose only cost is losing selection-box-from-on-top-of-a-node
— measured, not assumed: Shift does nothing else on that canvas. Left out
deliberately; `useTableSelection.ts` records the trade.

## The bug fix

`fix(dfd-editor): keep the caret in a table cell opened after the menu closes`
predates this branch. Using the cell context menu and then double-clicking a
cell to type dropped the caret ~400ms later, because Radix returns focus to the
trigger once the close animation finishes. The insert/delete menu had the same
problem; fill-then-type just makes it easy to hit.

## Verification

- `npx playwright test` — 28 passed, on this branch rebased onto current `main`.
  23 are new, in `frontend/src/features/dfd-editor/__tests__/e2e/table-node.spec.ts`,
  driven through the guest editor because it runs with no backend.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean at every commit in the series, not only the tip.
- `npx eslint` clean on every file touched. Pre-existing errors in
  `useDiagramState.ts` and `useParentRelationships.ts` are untouched.
- The gesture behaviour is covered by e2e rather than unit tests because whether
  a press lands on the table or on React Flow's drag depends on real event
  propagation, and nothing short of a browser answers it.

Note for anyone running these locally: Playwright had no browser installed in my
checkout, so `npx playwright install chromium` was needed first.

## Look hardest at

- The two-stage drag, as above.
- `useTableSelection.ts` hit-tests the DOM during a drag rather than measuring
  tracks. A row's rendered height is not knowable from the data — `minmax(h,
  auto)` lets it grow to fit wrapped text — so there is no sum to walk. It uses
  `elementsFromPoint` because the divider drag strips overlay the cells near
  every edge.

## Left out

- Deleting several rows or columns at once. An arrow key clears the grip's
  `axis` claim, so Delete stops being able to remove a row or column once the
  selection has moved or widened.
- Merged cells, per-cell text alignment and borders. The selection is the piece
  they all need and it is here; none of them is started.

pulls.title: feat(compose): rootless Podman overlay for local dev
pulls.body:
## Why this matters (plain language)

On locked-down enterprise or federal workstations, the developer often can't get `newuidmap`/`newgidmap` privileges required to run rootful Docker or a rootful Podman machine. That leaves them unable to run the standard `docker-compose.yml` locally — Postgres in particular fails on volume ownership. This PR adds a small, opt-in overlay that maps the Postgres container's UID to the host user so the shared stack Just Works under rootless Podman, without changing anything for the Docker-based flow.

## Value

- Widens who can contribute to Precogly (rootless Podman on managed laptops now works).
- Zero behavior change for the existing Docker workflow — the overlay is only applied when the developer opts in via `-f podman-compose.override.yml`.

## What this changes

- Adds `podman-compose.override.yml` that layers on top of `docker-compose.yml`:
  - `db.userns_mode` maps Postgres UID 70 to the host user so volume chowns succeed under rootless Podman.
  - A fully qualified Postgres image reference (Podman is strict about this).
- All other services and settings come from `docker-compose.yml` unchanged.
- Documents the one-time host configuration and overlay invocation in `docs/getting-started/local-podman.md`, registered in the mkdocs nav.

## Independence

- Local-dev only. No runtime code, no schema, no API surface. Does not depend on and is not depended on by any other open PR.

## Testing

- Verified the overlay boots the stack under rootless Podman on a host without subuid/subgid delegation.
- Docker-based `docker compose up` unchanged (overlay is not loaded by default).

pulls.title: fix: remove extent:'parent' that traps imported nodes inside trust zones
pulls.body:
Problem

When importing a third-party CycloneDX file (one without a precogly-dfd visualization), deserializeFromStructure sets extent: 'parent' on every node assigned to a zone. This tells React Flow to constrain the node within its parent's bounding box, preventing users from dragging nodes out of their trust zone.

The DFD editor's spatial reparenting system (useParentRelationships) is designed to handle containment via an all-4-corners check on drag stop, making extent: 'parent' both unnecessary and harmful. The only code that clears extent requires the node to leave its parent, but extent: 'parent' prevents it from leaving. Dead end.

The bug also persists through round-trips: the guest serializer does not strip extent from canvas_data, so exporting and reimporting a file carries the trapped state forward.

Fix

Four changes, all defensive-in-depth:

1. Remove extent: 'parent' from the import path (cyclonedx-guest.ts). Nodes no longer get the property on import.
2. Auto-size trust zones by child count (cyclonedx-guest.ts). Replaces the hardcoded 300px zone height with max(200, 50 + ceil(childCount / 2) * 120 + 80), so zones accommodate their children without overflow.
3. Clear stale extent in useParentRelationships (useParentRelationships.ts). If a node already has the correct parent but carries extent: 'parent', it gets cleared. This catches the bad state from any source: imports, old saved files, or future code paths. Narrowed to === 'parent' to avoid clearing custom coordinate extents.
4. Strip extent in the guest serializer (cyclonedx-guest.ts). Ensures extent never persists in saved files, breaking the round-trip infection chain.

Testing

- Import a third-party .cdx.json with zone-assigned assets. Verify nodes can be dragged between zones.
- Export from the guest editor, reimport. Verify nodes are still freely movable.
- Create a DFD from scratch, export, reimport. Verify no regression in the normal workflow.

pulls.title: feat: expand AWS library pack to 41 components with full taxonomy and compliance mappings
pulls.body:
## Summary

Expands the AWS threat library pack from 10 components covering 3 services into a comprehensive, evidence-based AWS threat modeling knowledge base covering 41 components across the most architecturally significant AWS services. Replaces the 3 legacy DFD templates with 9 new reference architecture templates grounded in published AWS architecture guidance.

### Why

Precogly's value proposition is that threats, countermeasures, and compliance mappings surface automatically as soon as components are placed on a data flow diagram. That only works when the library pack has meaningful coverage. The original AWS pack covered S3, Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, SQS, Bedrock, OpenSearch Serverless, Cognito, WAF, and CloudWatch. Real AWS architectures use dozens more services, and without library entries for them, users were left to define threats manually, losing the automation that makes Precogly useful.

This expansion was built in three batches, each validated against the pack schema before proceeding:

- **Batch 1 (Foundational Infrastructure):** IAM, VPC, EC2, RDS/Aurora, ELB, CloudTrail, KMS
- **Batch 2 (Containers, Secrets, Edge, DNS):** ECS, EKS, ECR, Secrets Manager, CloudFront, Route 53
- **Batch 3 (Final 18):** SNS, EventBridge, Step Functions, AppSync, ACM, EBS, CloudFormation, CodePipeline/CodeBuild, Elastic Beanstalk, SSM, GuardDuty, AWS Config, ElastiCache, Redshift, Security Hub, SageMaker, Bedrock Agents, Bedrock Knowledge Bases

### What changed

**Pack content (v3.0.0 to v4.0.0):**

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Components | 10 | 41 |
| Threats | 27 | 171 |
| Countermeasures | 46 | 188 (146 preventive, 39 detective, 3 corrective) |
| DFD templates | 3 (legacy) | 9 (new, legacy removed) |
| Icons | 9 | 41 (official AWS Architecture Icons) |

**Taxonomy join coverage:**

| Taxonomy | Coverage |
|---|---|
| STRIDE | 171/171 (100%) |
| CWE | 167/171 (98%) |
| MITRE ATT&CK | 160/171 (94%) |
| CAPEC | 99/171 (58%) |
| MITRE ATLAS | 18/171 (AI/ML threats only) |

**Compliance requirement join coverage:**

| Framework | Coverage |
|---|---|
| OWASP ASVS | 176/188 countermeasures (94%) |
| OWASP Top 10 | 155/188 (82%) |
| CRA | Mapped (sparse by design, 28 requirements available) |
| NIST CSF | Mapped (sparse by design, 4 requirements available) |
| SOC 2 | Mapped (sparse by design, 3 requirements available) |
| OWASP AISVS | 26 entries (AI/ML countermeasures only) |

**Schema migration:** All 188 countermeasures use `control_functions: [value]` (list format) to align with the control_functions/control_nature schema migration on main.

### DFD reference architecture templates

Each template is grounded in a published AWS reference architecture. Templates use `component_ref` links so that instantiating a template immediately inherits the full threat and countermeasure coverage from the pack.

| Template | File | AWS Source |
|---|---|---|
| Serverless Web App | `aws-serverless-web-app.yaml` | [Lambda Web Application Reference Architecture](https://aws.amazon.com/lambda/resources/refarch/refarch-webapp/) |
| Three-Tier Web App | `aws-three-tier-web-app.yaml` | [Web Application Hosting Best Practices](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/web-application-hosting-best-practices/an-overview-of-traditional-web-hosting.html) |
| Containerized Microservices | `aws-containerized-microservices.yaml` | [AWS Containers Architecture Hub](https://aws.amazon.com/architecture/containers/) |
| Event-Driven Pipeline | `aws-event-driven-pipeline.yaml` | [Event-Driven Architectures with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/concepts-event-driven-architectures.html) |
| Security Baseline (SRA) | `aws-security-baseline.yaml` | [AWS Security Reference Architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/security-reference-architecture/welcome.html) |
| SaaS Tenant Isolation | `aws-saas-multi-tenant.yaml` | [SaaS Tenant Isolation Architecture Patterns](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/saas-solutions-tenant-isolation-architectures/saas-solutions-tenant-isolation-architecture-patterns.html) |
| Data Lake & Analytics | `aws-data-lake-analytics.yaml` | [Building Data Lakes on AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-data-lakes/building-data-lake-aws.html) |
| RAG / Generative AI | `aws-rag-genai.yaml` | [Generative AI Application Builder](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/solutions/latest/generative-ai-application-builder-on-aws/architecture-overview.html), [Well-Architected Agentic AI Lens](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/agentic-ai-lens/agentic-ai-lens.html) |
| CI/CD Pipeline | `aws-cicd-pipeline.yaml` | [CI/CD Pipeline with CodePipeline and CDK](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/set-up-a-ci-cd-pipeline-by-using-aws-codepipeline-and-aws-cdk.html) |

**Removed legacy templates:** `s3-lambda.yaml`, `aws-serverless.yaml`, `aws-ai-chatbot.yaml` (superseded by the new templates above).

### Threat sourcing methodology

Threats are derived from authoritative AWS security material, not invented:

- **AWS Security Hub controls and Foundational Security Best Practices (FSBP):** primary source for service-specific security safeguards
- **Stratus Red Team:** granular, per-service AWS attack techniques with direct MITRE ATT&CK mappings
- **CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark:** prescriptive, auditable controls
- **AWS service security documentation:** each service's "Security in..." chapter
- **AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar**

Threats focus on design-level and architectural problems visible on a data flow diagram (trust boundary crossings, data flow exposure, privilege escalation paths, blast radius), not individual resource misconfigurations that automated scanners already catch.

### Merge notes

This branch has 5 files that conflict with main due to concurrent changes:
- `countermeasures.yaml`: main migrated existing entries to `control_functions`; this branch added new entries and migrated all of them
- `bedrock.svg`: main updated the icon; take main's version
- `aws-ai-chatbot.yaml` and `s3-lambda.yaml`: main added `technology` fields; this branch deletes both files
- `seed.py`: main added Risk Register seeding; this branch updated template slugs. Changes are in different sections.

pulls.title: feat(dfd-editor): add a table node to the canvas
pulls.body:
Part of #520.

## Problem

There is no way to lay out tabular content on a DFD canvas — a PMV/context matrix, a STRIDE-per-element grid, a pros/cons comparison next to the diagram it belongs to. Today that means a screenshot, a sticky note, or leaving for another tool.

It is also the single most-requested missing feature in comparable editors: excalidraw#4847 has been open since 2022 with 147 comments, several of them people saying they moved to Lucid, Whimsical or Microsoft Whiteboard over this one gap.

## What this does

Adds a `table` node type. It is an annotation, like the sticky note: no DFD semantics, excluded from threat analysis.

- Text cells that wrap, edited in place, with Tab / Shift-Tab / Enter moving between them and Shift-Enter inserting a line break
- Drag any column or row divider to resize, including the outer edges. A row's stored height is a floor rather than a fixed height, so a row grows when its text needs more — Miro's rule
- Clicking **Table** in the component panel opens a grid picker — hover to size, or switch to an input mode that keeps the grid as a live preview and reaches sizes the 8×8 grid cannot express. Dragging the palette entry still drops a default 3×3
- Grips along the top and left edges select a row or column; right-clicking any cell or grip offers insert above/below/left/right and delete; Delete removes the selected row or column
- Corner handles scale the whole table. Shift constrains to a uniform factor and scales cell text with it, matching Miro
- Column/row steppers and a header-row toggle in the edit panel
- Renders in PNG and SVG export and in the read-only viewer, since `export-diagram-image.ts` runs `html-to-image` over the live DOM

## Where the code is

| file | what |
|---|---|
| `components/nodes/TableNode.tsx` | the node: grid, cells, editing, selection, context menu |
| `hooks/useTableDrag.ts` | both pointer gestures — divider resize and corner scale |
| `components/nodes/table-chrome.tsx` | geometry constants, the row/column grip, the small action buttons |
| `types/diagram.ts` | `TableNodeData` and the pure insert/remove/resize functions |

`TableNode` started at 770 lines against 249 for the next largest file in `nodes/`, and is now 465. Some of the remainder is intrinsic — every other node there renders a shape with a label, this one does grid layout, in-cell editing, keyboard navigation, two pointer gestures, a selection model and a context menu.

The cell and its context menu stay inline deliberately: extracting them costs eight props to move a hundred lines, and that contract reads worse than the version it replaces.

## Alternatives rejected

**`NodeResizer` for the corner handles**, as `StickyNoteNode` uses. It wants to own `style.width`/`height`, and this table's size is derived from its column widths and row heights. Two owners of one dimension start disagreeing, so the corner drag is hand-rolled and writes the widths instead.

**A `ResizeObserver` feeding real row heights back to absolutely positioned overlays.** Once a row can grow past its stored height, any control positioned from a running sum of stored heights drifts off the row it belongs to. Measuring keeps that arithmetic and adds a frame where the overlays are stale. Instead the grips and dividers are grid items in the same tracks as the cells, pushing their visible parts outside with `bottom: 100%` / `right: 100%` — which deletes the arithmetic and makes the misalignment impossible rather than corrected.

**Free-text column/row counts in the edit panel.** Committing per keystroke walks every prefix of what is typed, so 3 → 12 would commit `1` first and truncate nine columns of content. Committing on blur instead means the canvas shows nothing until focus leaves the field. Steppers have neither problem. The grid picker *does* use free text, because nothing exists yet to truncate.

**A cap on table size.** Deliberately unbounded. The cost is real and unpaid for: no virtualization, so a 20×200 table is 4000 DOM nodes the canvas walks on every pan and zoom. If that bites, the fix is virtualizing the cell grid.

## Worth reviewing hardest

- **Zoom correction**, `useTableDrag.ts`. Both gestures divide pointer deltas by `getZoom()`, because sizes are stored in diagram coordinates. Get this wrong and dragging at 50% zoom moves half as far as the cursor — it is what most of the draw.io column-resize bug list is about.
- **The three node registries.** `nodeTypes`, `canvasNodeTypes` and `guestNodeTypes` now assert exhaustiveness with `satisfies Record<DiagramNodeType, unknown>`. Without it React Flow silently substitutes its default node for an unregistered type, which renders as a small box containing the label and reads as a broken component rather than a missing entry. Not hypothetical — it is defect 1 below.
- **Grid placement**, `TableNode.tsx`. Every cell, grip and divider is placed explicitly. A column divider spans `1 / -1` of its column, so between them the overlays claim every defined cell; anything left to auto-placement lands in implicit rows below the table. Defect 2 below.
- **Double-click propagation.** A cell's `onDoubleClick` stops propagation so it never reaches `handleNodeDoubleClick`, which sets `isInlineEditing` on the node. That flag is the fresh-drop hook meaning "caret in the first cell", and without the guard every double-click bounced editing back to cell 1.
- **Two set-during-render blocks** in `TableNode`, seeding the caret and clearing the axis selection. Both derive local state from a changed prop. They were `useEffect`s that had been violating `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` all along — extracting a second component into the file stopped the React Compiler lint bailing out and it started reporting them.

## Verification

```
npx tsc -b        # clean
npm run build     # clean
npx eslint <every changed file>   # clean
```

Each commit typechecks on its own, checked by building at each SHA. Pre-existing and untouched: one `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` error at `DFDEditor.tsx:134` and several in the guest-editor tree, all in code this branch does not modify.

This frontend has no test tooling — no vitest, jest or testing-library — so the rest is manual. It has been exercised in the editor, which found and fixed three defects that compiling could not see:

1. The table rendered as a single small box. `guestNodeTypes` had no `table` entry, so React Flow substituted its default node.
2. Rows collapsed to a thin strip under an empty box. The overlays' explicit grid placement claimed every defined cell, pushing the auto-placed cells into implicit rows.
3. Wrapping only took effect on blur. The editing textarea was fixed at one line and scrolled internally, so the row had nothing to grow around until the plain span took over.

Not individually confirmed: divider and corner drags at a non-100% zoom, shift-uniform scaling, the context menu on every entry, and Delete on a selected axis. The refactor landed after that browser pass, so it is compile-verified only.

## Not included

Cell fill colour, markdown/CSV paste and copy, merged cells, drag-to-reorder, multi-cell selection. All tracked with rationale and ordering in #520.

## Compatibility

No breaking changes. `fontSize` on the node data is optional so tables saved before it keep rendering at the previous size, and cells are objects rather than bare strings from the start so that a cell can later hold a diagram node without migrating saved diagrams.

Adds one dependency: `@radix-ui/react-context-menu`, alongside the 15 Radix packages already present.

pulls.title: Fix Vercel errors

pulls.body:

pulls.title: fix(threat-models): paginate the Risk Register
pulls.body:
## The problem

`useRisks` extracted `results` from the paginated response and discarded `count` and `next`. A register of 24 risks loaded 20 and reported 20 in the header. The remaining four were unreachable, and selection and bulk actions operated on the first page without saying so.

Closes #484.

## What changed

**Backend.** `ClientSizedPagination` sets `page_size_query_param` and `max_page_size = 200`, and becomes the project default. Stock `PageNumberPagination` leaves `page_size_query_param` unset, so `PAGE_SIZE` was the only page size any client could get, and subclassing is the only way DRF offers to change that. A caller that asks for no size still gets `PAGE_SIZE`, so no existing endpoint changes shape.

**Frontend.** `getPage<T>()` in `lib/api.ts` returns the whole `Page` and reports a bare array as a single complete page, so callers never branch on which shape came back. `useRisks` takes `{ page, pageSize }`, keys the query on both, and uses `placeholderData: keepPreviousData`. Page keys extend the existing `list` key, so every mutation's `invalidateQueries` still reaches all cached pages unchanged. The header reports `count`.

**Seeds.** No seeded threat model carried any risks, so the register was empty in every development database and its pagination could not be exercised at all. `_seed_risks` adds 24 to the first sample model, keyed on whether that model already has risks rather than on whether this run created it — `_create_sample_threat_models` skips a model that exists, so a step hung off model creation would never run on a database that had been seeded before.

## The trade-off to look at hardest

The board paginates with the table rather than fetching every page. A Kanban column therefore counts only the current page, so an empty column does not mean no risks carry that response. A banner says as much and the page-size selector goes to 200, but the caveat is real and was chosen deliberately over two alternatives:

- **Fetch every page.** Keeps the board, select-all and the counts correct by construction, at the cost of unbounded rows in the DOM. The CycloneDX and tm_library importers create risks in a loop, so a register can be large.
- **Per-column server queries.** Correct and bounded, but needs `response` added to `filterset_fields` plus an `isnull` escape for the untriaged column, and five queries per board load.

Selection is page-scoped, which the bulk bar now states outright. Deleting a page's last row steps back a page first, because DRF answers an out-of-range page with a 404 rather than an empty one.

## Verification

```
$ uv run pytest -q
323 passed, 7 subtests passed

$ uv run pytest apps/threats/tests/test_risk_pagination.py -q
5 passed
```

Reverting the settings line to stock `PageNumberPagination` fails two of the five (`AssertionError: 20 != 24`), so those two gate the change rather than only describing it. The other three pass either way and pin the DRF behavior the frontend now depends on.

Against the seeded database:

```
default        -> count=24 rows=20 next=yes
?page=2        -> count=24 rows=4  next=no
?page_size=50  -> count=24 rows=24 next=no
```

That first line is the reproduction in #484 verbatim.

```
$ npm run build
✓ 2619 modules transformed
✓ built in 3.46s
```

**The UI itself is not verified.** This repo has no frontend tests and I have not clicked through the register in a browser. `tsc -b` and the bundle are clean; whether the page renders correctly is unchecked.

## Left out

`components/ui/pagination.tsx` is upstream shadcn v4 with its two import paths rewritten. `npx shadcn add pagination` was not used: it resolves upstream's `cn` import as an npm package and installs an unrelated `cn@0.2.6`, and prompts to overwrite `button.tsx`.

Thirteen other API modules share the `results`-and-discard shape. Nine viewsets set `pagination_class = None`, so every library, taxonomy and pack list is unaffected by it. The rest are follow-ups rather than scope here, tracked in #514.

No breaking changes.

issue.title: feat(cyclonedx): complete satisfies/externalReferences import + POA&M tracking
issue.body:
## Why this matters (plain language)

Precogly can already import CycloneDX Threat-Model BOMs (TM-BOMs), but the importer today drops several fields that FedRAMP / SSPP-style workflows depend on: which NIST control a countermeasure claims to satisfy, the evidence URL for each control, and Plan-of-Action-and-Milestones (POA&M) tracking (`poam:id`, scheduled completion date, whether a control is overdue). Users generating a TM-BOM from a compliance tool and importing it into Precogly currently lose that context and have to re-enter it by hand.

This PR closes those gaps so a TM-BOM round-trips through Precogly with its compliance and POA&M metadata intact.

## Value

- Enables using Precogly as the visualization/threat-analysis layer for teams whose source of truth is a CycloneDX TM-BOM (GSA SSPP flow, FedRAMP submissions, etc.) without losing control-mapping fidelity.
- Adds first-class POA&M fields on `InstanceCountermeasure`, so overdue controls surface in the API without a custom join.

## What this changes

- **POA&M fields on `InstanceCountermeasure`**: `poam_id`, `scheduled_completion`, and a `source` enum (`manual` / `vault_import` / `pentest`), plus a `days_overdue` property that ignores `IMPLEMENTED` / `VERIFIED` controls. The CycloneDX importer parses `poam:id` and `poam:scheduled-completion` control properties.
- **`satisfies[]` import**: imports `definitions[].requirements`, creates `InstanceCountermeasureStandard` rows for each control's `satisfies[]`, resolving `StandardRequirement` FK when the framework is installed. When the framework isn't installed, we keep section_code / framework_name / description snapshots so the mapping still displays and round-trips on export. Dangling references warn and skip. Multiple unresolved mappings per control are all preserved (previously only the last survived).
- **`externalReferences` import**: a control externalReference typed `evidence` populates `InstanceCountermeasure.evidence_url`.
- **`crosses_trust_zone`**: `DataFlow` imported from `blueprint.flows` sets `crosses_trust_zone` when source and destination sit in different trust zones.
- Refactors requirement-snapshot construction into a single helper.

Closes tracking issues in GSA-TTS/TTSE-petrified-forest-sspp#31.

## Independence

- Migration `threats/0015_poam_fields` is additive and independent (numbered above current `main`'s `threats/0014`).
- Files touched are disjoint from PRs #560 (packs/systems/frontend icon), #561 (compliance app), and #551 (docker-compose overlay). Safe to merge in any order relative to those.

## Testing

- `backend/apps/threats/tests/test_poam_fields.py` — POA&M model fields, `days_overdue`, API filters.
- `backend/apps/threat_models/tests/test_cdx_poam_import.py` — CycloneDX `poam:*` property parsing on import.
- `backend/apps/threat_models/tests/test_cdx_import_audit.py` — resolved/unresolved/dangling satisfies, evidence-url mapping, zone-crossing flags, satisfies round-trip.
- Full backend suite: `345 passed` (no regressions).
- `manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run`: no missing migrations.
- `ruff check`: clean.

## Draft note

Marked draft — awaiting a first pass of upstream review on the `satisfies[]` snapshot-vs-resolved contract (do we prefer snapshot-only when the framework isn't installed, or block the import?). Happy to switch behavior if reviewers want stricter semantics.

issue.body: ## Why this matters (plain language) Precogly's DFD nodes render a technology icon next to the node label — for example, an S3 bucket shows an S3 logo. Today only individual components in a pack can declare an icon; the pack itself can't. That means threat libraries and template packs (which have a strong brand identity — "AWS", "Azure", "OWASP") show a generic square in the UI, and components without their own icon have no visual context for which pack they came from. This PR gives packs a first-class icon field and lets components without their own icon fall back to their pack's icon. Everything renders through the existing safe base64-`` pipeline introduced by the #516 XSS fix — no new rendering path and no new npm dependency. ## Value - Restores brand context in the DFD editor (AWS pack components look like AWS things even if a specific service has no bespoke icon yet). - Same XSS-safety guarantee as the existing per-component icon mechanism — pack-supplied SVGs are never injected as raw HTML. - No new frontend dependency. No new backend dependency. Migration is a single additive `TextField`. ## Context on the earlier attempt An earlier branch (`feature/icon-library-mvp`) tried to add pack icons by introducing `@thesvg/react`, a JSON icon config (slug / variant / className / style), and raw-SVG-component rendering. It was written before #516 landed. Merging it as-is would (a) re-introduce a raw-markup icon rendering path that #516 deliberately removed, and (b) run two incompatible icon pipelines side-by-side. This PR keeps the value (pack + component-level fallback) by extending the *existing, already-reviewed* mechanism one level up, from component to pack. Not carried over: per-component icon JSONField overrides, vendor-brand-logo resolution via `@thesvg/react`, and the dual vendor+service icon render. Re-adding equivalents needs a fresh design that keeps the base64-`` constraint. Happy to scope that as a follow-up. ## What this changes **Backend** - `LibraryPack.icon_svg` (`TextField`, same shape as `ComponentLibrary.icon_svg`), migration `packs/0003_librarypack_icon_svg`. - Pack importer reads an optional `pack.yaml` `icon: ` (relative to the pack dir), mirroring the existing per-component `icon: ` convention in `components.yaml`. Safe to merge in any order relative to those. ## Testing - Backend: `ruff check` clean; new `apps/packs/test_pack_icon_svg.py` (4 tests) + full `apps/packs`, `apps/systems`, and template-pack-visibility suite (51 total) pass; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports no changes. - Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on touched files.

issue.title: feat(packs): pack-level icon via safe SVG-file loading
issue.body: ## Why this matters (plain language) Precogly's DFD nodes render a technology icon next to the node label — for example, an S3 bucket shows an S3 logo. Today only individual components in a pack can declare an icon; the pack itself can't. That means threat libraries and template packs (which have a strong brand identity — "AWS", "Azure", "OWASP") show a generic square in the UI, and components without their own icon have no visual context for which pack they came from. This PR gives packs a first-class icon field and lets components without their own icon fall back to their pack's icon. Everything renders through the existing safe base64-`` pipeline introduced by the #516 XSS fix — no new rendering path and no new npm dependency. ## Value - Restores brand context in the DFD editor (AWS pack components look like AWS things even if a specific service has no bespoke icon yet). - Same XSS-safety guarantee as the existing per-component icon mechanism — pack-supplied SVGs are never injected as raw HTML. - No new frontend dependency. No new backend dependency. Migration is a single additive `TextField`. ## Context on the earlier attempt An earlier branch (`feature/icon-library-mvp`) tried to add pack icons by introducing `@thesvg/react`, a JSON icon config (slug / variant / className / style), and raw-SVG-component rendering. It was written before #516 landed. Merging it as-is would (a) re-introduce a raw-markup icon rendering path that #516 deliberately removed, and (b) run two incompatible icon pipelines side-by-side. This PR keeps the value (pack + component-level fallback) by extending the *existing, already-reviewed* mechanism one level up, from component to pack. Not carried over: per-component icon JSONField overrides, vendor-brand-logo resolution via `@thesvg/react`, and the dual vendor+service icon render. Re-adding equivalents needs a fresh design that keeps the base64-`` constraint. Happy to scope that as a follow-up. ## What this changes **Backend** - `LibraryPack.icon_svg` (`TextField`, same shape as `ComponentLibrary.icon_svg`), migration `packs/0003_librarypack_icon_svg`. - Pack importer reads an optional `pack.yaml` `icon: ` (relative to the pack dir), mirroring the existing per-component `icon: ` convention in `components.yaml`. Missing files warn; nothing throws. - `LibraryPackListSerializer` / `LibraryPackDetailSerializer` expose `icon_svg` (viewset is `ReadOnlyModelViewSet`, so no write path is added). - `ComponentLibrarySerializer` gains `source_pack_icon_svg` so a component without its own icon can fall back to its pack's icon. **Frontend** - `ComponentLibraryItem.sourcePackIconSvg`; `transformToTechnology` and `ComponentPanel` fall back to it. - Everything still flows through the existing `SvgIcon` component (base64 data-URI ``, never `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`). **Docs** - `creating-library-packs.md` documents the `pack.yaml` `icon:` key and explains why it's safe. ## Independence - Migration `packs/0003_librarypack_icon_svg` is additive and independent. - Files touched are disjoint from PRs #559 (threats/cyclonedx), #561 (compliance app), and #551 (docker-compose overlay). Safe to merge in any order relative to those. ## Testing - Backend: `ruff check` clean; new `apps/packs/test_pack_icon_svg.py` (4 tests) + full `apps/packs`, `apps/systems`, and template-pack-visibility suite (51 total) pass; `makemigrations --check --dry-run` reports no changes. - Frontend: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on touched files.

556.message:
feat(dfd-editor): merge table cells

Select a range and merge it, so a table can carry a header spanning the
columns under it. That is what a STRIDE-per-interaction worksheet needs
(#520): a component name over its Mitigations/Weaknesses pair.

Spans live on the anchor cell as `colSpan`/`rowSpan`, absent meaning one.
The cells a merge swallows stay in the array so the grid stays rectangular
and every index into it still means what it did; which cells are covered is
derived from the anchors rather than flagged, because a flag and the span it
mirrors are two things that can disagree. This also answers the open
question in #520: a span composes with a later field pointing at a child
node, so a cell that both spans and contains is just an anchor with both.

Behaviour follows what the tools actually do, checked 2026-09-16. Miro's
interaction: select, then Merge cells on the context menu, unmergeable at
any time. Excel's content rule: the anchor keeps its text and the rest are
emptied. No confirmation, unlike Excel and Sheets, because undo restores the
text here and the table already discards cells without asking when a row or
column is removed.

An insert or delete through a merge unmerges it. Neither spreadsheet does
better: Excel expands the selection to the merge's full extent, so inserting
one row inside a ten-row merge inserts ten, and Sheets often refuses the
insert outright. Both leave people doing unmerge / edit / re-merge by hand,
which is what this does for them.

Two things merging broke, fixed here:

Divider drag strips span the whole table, so the strip for the boundary
between two merged rows lay across the middle of the merged cell and took
clicks meant for it — a two-row-tall cell has it running through exactly
where a pointer lands. Dividers are now emitted in runs that skip any
boundary a merge crosses.

Arrow keys stepped onto covered cells, which render nothing, so the
selection appeared to vanish. The covered map carries each cell's anchor,
and `moveFocus` steps out of the whole block rather than one cell.

feat(libraries): add a STRIDE per Interaction worksheet pack

A workshop grid as a canvas table: two elements and the flow between them,
a row per STRIDE category, a Mitigations / Weaknesses pair per element.
Asked for in #520 — facilitators rebuild this by hand every session.

`pack_type: template` already existed in the model and no shipped pack used
it, so this needs no migration. Pack discovery is `rglob("pack.yaml")` with
explicit support for categorized layouts, so the new top-level `worksheets/`
category needs no code either. The pack carries no components, threats or
countermeasures: a worksheet is a method, not a technology domain, so it has
nothing to feed the suggestion engine and nothing to join to a taxonomy.

The greyed cells are load-bearing, not decoration. They are the STRIDE
categories that do not apply to an element of that type, from Vikram's
heuristic in #520 — external entities are not tampered with, data flows are
not spoofed. Grey therefore *means* "not applicable" here, which is why the
header rows are yellow: a grey header would read as a ruled-out column.

Verified against a running stack rather than by reading the code path:
validator returns success, import creates the template, spans and fills
survive the CamelCase renderer unchanged, and inserting it from the
Templates browser puts 52 cells on the canvas — 56 less the 4 the merges
cover.

fix(diagrams): offer a template pack's templates without connecting it

A pack's templates only appeared once the pack was joined to the threat
model, so importing the STRIDE worksheet pack was not enough — the browser
said "No templates found" with no hint that an unconnected pack was sitting
there. A facilitator had to connect a worksheet to their threat model as
though it described their stack.

The gate exists so that `component_ref`s resolve: the `resolved` action
turns them into component_library ids, and an AWS template inserted without
the AWS pack yields components pointing at nothing. A pack of `pack_type:
template` ships no components at all, so nothing in its templates can fail
to resolve and a connection has nothing to supply. Those are exempt; every
other pack is gated exactly as before, which the test pins in both
directions.

Found by inserting the pack against a running stack. Reading the path does
not show it — every hop from pack YAML to canvas is a passthrough, and this
sits in a queryset upstream of all of them. Confirmed by ablation: with the
clause reverted the worksheet disappears from the browser again.

fix(dfd-editor): dismiss the context menu when a cell is pressed

A selected table swallowed the pointerdown on its cells, so an open context
menu stayed open until a click landed outside the table. An unselected one
was fine, because only a selected table takes the pointer at all.

React's stopPropagation stops the native event at the root container, and
Radix dismisses layers from a pointerdown listener on document above it, so
the menu never learned the press had happened. Nothing needed the stop:
nodrag is what keeps a press from dragging the node, and no ancestor of a
cell handles pointerdown.

The same stop on the cell textarea goes with it. It cannot strand a menu —
opening one blurs the textarea and unmounts it, so the two are never open at
once — but it bought nothing either.

issue.title: feat(dfd-editor): merge table cells and STRIDE worksheet template
issue.body:
Three things that belong together: merging cells, the worksheet that needed
merging, and a context-menu bug the cell selection in #553 shipped with.

Select a range and merge it, so a table can carry a header spanning the columns
under it. That is what a STRIDE-per-interaction worksheet needs (#520): a
component name over its Mitigations/Weaknesses pair, which is the layout Vikram
posted and the reason this exists. That worksheet now ships as a template pack
rather than living only in my checkout.

Screenshot of the rebuilt worksheet is at `frontend/tmp/stride-merged.png` in my
checkout if you want it dropped in here; I can't attach images from the CLI.

## Behaviour, and where it comes from

Checked against the tools on 2026-09-16 rather than guessed.

**Interaction is Miro's** — select cells, *Merge cells* on the context menu, and
they can be unmerged at any time.

**Content is Excel's rule** — the anchor keeps its text, the rest are emptied.
[Microsoft](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/merge-and-unmerge-cells-in-excel):
"the contents of only one cell (the upper-left cell…) appear in the merged cell.
The contents of the other cells that you merge are deleted." Sheets is the same.

**No confirmation, unlike both of them.** They warn because in Excel and Sheets
the discarded text is gone for good — Microsoft's doc is explicit that unmerge
does not bring it back. Undo restores it here, and the table already discards
cells without asking when a row or column is removed, with the panel saying so:
*"Removing a column or row discards its cells. Undo restores them."*

**An insert or delete through a merge unmerges it.** Neither spreadsheet does
anything better. Excel expands the selection to the merge's full extent, so
inserting one row inside a ten-row merge inserts
[ten](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5033930/insert-columns-rows-where-there-are-merged-cells);
Sheets often refuses the insert outright. In both, the documented workaround is
unmerge → edit → re-merge, which is what this does for you. Notion does not
support merging at all.

## Data model

Spans live on the anchor as `colSpan`/`rowSpan`, absent meaning one, so a diagram
saved before merging existed is already correct. The cells a merge swallows stay
in the array, keeping the grid rectangular so every index into it still means
what it did. Which cells are covered is **derived** from the anchors, not
flagged — a flag and the span it mirrors are two things that can disagree.

This also answers the open question in #520. A span composes with a later field
pointing at a child node, so a cell that both spans and contains is just an
anchor carrying both. The two features do not need settling together.

## The worksheet

`libraries/packs/worksheets/stride-worksheets`, one template: **STRIDE per
Interaction**. Two elements and the flow between them, a row per STRIDE
category, a Mitigations/Weaknesses pair per element.

**Greyed cells are semantic, not styling** — the categories that do not apply to
that element type, from Vikram's heuristic in #520 (external entity: T, I, D, E;
data store: S, E; data flow: S, R, E; process: none). Grey therefore means "not
applicable" throughout the worksheet, which is why the header rows are yellow: a
grey header would read as a struck-out row.

**`pack_type: template`, not `full`.** It carries no components, threats or
countermeasures. A worksheet is a method rather than a technology domain, so it
has nothing to contribute to the suggestion engine and nothing to join against a
taxonomy — it is complete as it stands, not an unfinished pack.

## Template packs are offered without being connected

`DFDTemplatesLibraryViewSet.get_queryset` gated every template on its source
pack being connected to the threat model, so the `component_ref`s in it resolve;
an AWS template inserted without the AWS pack yields components pointing at
nothing. A template pack ships no components, so a connection has nothing to
supply, and gating it would make a facilitator connect a STRIDE worksheet to
their model as though it described their stack. Those packs are now exempt.

I traced the path from pack YAML to canvas and called it a passthrough before
finding this, which was wrong — the gate sits in a queryset upstream of every
hop I looked at. It only turned up by inserting the template against a running
stack.

## Bugs fixed here

**Merged cells were not clickable through the middle.** Divider drag strips span
the whole table, so the strip for the boundary between two merged rows lay across
the centre of the merged cell — exactly where a pointer lands — and started a row
resize instead. Dividers are now emitted in runs that skip any boundary a merge
crosses. Found by a test timing out on `cursor-row-resize … intercepts pointer
events`; it would have shipped otherwise.

**Arrow keys walked into merged blocks.** Stepping right from a two-wide merge
landed on a covered cell, which renders nothing, so the selection appeared to
vanish. The covered map carries each cell's anchor, and `moveFocus` steps out of
the whole block rather than one cell at a time.

**The context menu would not close over a selected table** — this one shipped in
#553. A selected table swallowed the pointerdown on its cells, so an open menu
stayed open until a click landed outside the table; an unselected one was fine,
since only a selected table takes the pointer at all. React's `stopPropagation`
stops the native event at the root container, and Radix dismisses layers from a
`pointerdown` listener on `document` above it. Nothing needed the stop: `nodrag`
is what keeps a press from dragging the node, and no ancestor of a cell handles
`pointerdown` (@xyflow/react 12.10.0 — its only React-level one is on `Handle`, a
descendant, and the pane's is capture-phase).

## Verification

- `npx playwright test` — 36 passed, including a regression test for the menu
  that fails on the previous commit (`toBeHidden` → received visible).
- `manage.py test apps.diagrams.tests.test_template_pack_visibility` — 2 passed,
  covering both halves: the template pack is offered unconnected, and every other
  pack is still gated.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint` clean on every file touched.
- Inserted the worksheet from the template browser against a running stack, with
  the pack imported and deliberately not connected to any threat model — the
  state a real user is in.

## Look hardest at

- `expandRangeOverMerges`. Merging a range that cuts an existing merge would
  leave two anchors claiming one cell, which nothing downstream can render. It
  grows the range to swallow whole merges, iterated to a fixed point because
  widening to absorb one can bring the edge against another.
- The queryset relaxation. Widening it further would break technology templates
  quietly, which is why the second test matters more than the first.
- The divider runs, which are the least obvious part of the diff and exist only
  because of the click-stealing bug above.

## Left out

- Merging is not offered across a selection that is already partly merged in a
  way the expansion cannot resolve; it simply widens instead. No case found where
  that is wrong, but it is the area I would fuzz first.
- The guest editor gets no templates, deliberately, so the worksheet is not

which is what this does for them.

Divider drag strips span the whole table, so the strip for the boundary
between two merged rows lay across the middle of the merged cell and took

issue.title: feat(dfd-editor): select and fill table cells
issue.body:
Canvas tables could only carry text. This adds a cell selection and a colour
fill on top of it, so a row can be marked as the risky one — the first thing
anyone reaches for in a threat model.

Builds on the table node from #<!-- canvas-table-node -->, already on `main`.

## What's here

Six commits, each self-contained:

| commit | |
|---|---|
| `chore(ui)` | context menu submenu primitives, matching shadcn's canonical output |
| `fix(dfd-editor)` | a pre-existing focus bug, see below |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | select cells — click, drag, row/column grips |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | fill them with a colour |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | arrow keys move the selection, shift-arrow extends it |
| `feat(dfd-editor)` | the picker shows what the selection already carries |

## Decisions, and what was rejected

**Two-stage drag.** An unselected table drags from anywhere in its body like
every other node; once selected, a press on a cell belongs to the table and the
table moves from its grips. The alternative was a dedicated always-visible drag
border, which costs an affordance on every table and breaks "grab the middle and
move it" outright. This is the Miro rule. It is the change most likely to feel
wrong in the hand, so it is the thing to try first.

`nodrag` on the cells is what enforces it — not the `stopPropagation` in the
hook. React Flow drags from a native listener on the node wrapper, which has
already run by the time a React handler on a descendant fires. The first version
used `stopPropagation` alone and the table moved along with the selection drag.

**Fill is stored per cell**, not per row or column. So a row inserted into a
filled column arrives unfilled, which is visible. The alternative was resolving
cell over column over row on every render and giving "clear this cell" two
meanings.

**The eight colours** are the intersection of Notion's, Google Sheets' and
Airtable's palettes, checked 2026-09-16. Brown is Notion-only; cyan and teal are
absent from Notion; these eight are in all three. Five of the values are already
the sticky note tints, so a yellow cell matches a yellow sticky note beside it —
`TABLE_FILL_COLORS` records that the two sets have to move together, and that
they are frozen Tailwind v3 values while the project runs v4.

**Gray is slate-200, not slate-100.** The header row paints itself slate-100, so
a slate-100 gray would be invisible on row 0 and would read as a second header
row anywhere else.

**No shift-click to extend**, though every spreadsheet has one. Shift is React
Flow's `selectionKeyCode` and a pointerdown under it never reaches the cell;
measured on the guest canvas, Alt and Meta get through and Shift does not.
Keydowns are untouched, which is why shift-*arrow* works. Restoring shift-click
means `selectionKeyCode={null}` on the ReactFlow in `DFDEditor` and
`GuestDFDEditor`, whose only cost is losing selection-box-from-on-top-of-a-node
— measured, not assumed: Shift does nothing else on that canvas. Left out
deliberately; `useTableSelection.ts` records the trade.

## The bug fix

`fix(dfd-editor): keep the caret in a table cell opened after the menu closes`
predates this branch. Using the cell context menu and then double-clicking a
cell to type dropped the caret ~400ms later, because Radix returns focus to the
trigger once the close animation finishes. The insert/delete menu had the same
problem; fill-then-type just makes it easy to hit.

## Verification

- `npx playwright test` — 28 passed, on this branch rebased onto current `main`.
  23 are new, in `frontend/src/features/dfd-editor/__tests__/e2e/table-node.spec.ts`,
  driven through the guest editor because it runs with no backend.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean at every commit in the series, not only the tip.
- `npx eslint` clean on every file touched. Pre-existing errors in
  `useDiagramState.ts` and `useParentRelationships.ts` are untouched.
- The gesture behaviour is covered by e2e rather than unit tests because whether
  a press lands on the table or on React Flow's drag depends on real event
  propagation, and nothing short of a browser answers it.

Note for anyone running these locally: Playwright had no browser installed in my
checkout, so `npx playwright install chromium` was needed first.

## Look hardest at

- The two-stage drag, as above.
- `useTableSelection.ts` hit-tests the DOM during a drag rather than measuring
  tracks. A row's rendered height is not knowable from the data — `minmax(h,
  auto)` lets it grow to fit wrapped text — so there is no sum to walk. It uses
  `elementsFromPoint` because the divider drag strips overlay the cells near
  every edge.

## Left out

- Deleting several rows or columns at once. An arrow key clears the grip's
  `axis` claim, so Delete stops being able to remove a row or column once the
  selection has moved or widened.
- Merged cells, per-cell text alignment and borders. The selection is the piece

feat(libraries): add a STRIDE per Interaction worksheet pack

A workshop grid as a canvas table: two elements and the flow between them,
a row per STRIDE category, a Mitigations / Weaknesses pair per element.
Asked for in #520 — facilitators rebuild this by hand every session.

`pack_type: template` already existed in the model and no shipped pack used
it, so this needs no migration. Pack discovery is `rglob("pack.yaml")` with
explicit support for categorized layouts, so the new top-level `worksheets/`
category needs no code either. The pack carries no components, threats or
countermeasures: a worksheet is a method, not a technology domain, so it has
nothing to feed the suggestion engine and nothing to join to a taxonomy.

The greyed cells are load-bearing, not decoration. They are the STRIDE
categories that do not apply to an element of that type, from Vikram's
heuristic in #520 — external entities are not tampered with, data flows are
not spoofed. Grey therefore *means* "not applicable" here, which is why the
header rows are yellow: a grey header would read as a ruled-out column.

Verified against a running stack rather than by reading the code path:
validator returns success, import creates the template, spans and fills
survive the CamelCase renderer unchanged, and inserting it from the
Templates browser puts 52 cells on the canvas — 56 less the 4 the merges
cover.

fix(diagrams): offer a template pack's templates without connecting it

A pack's templates only appeared once the pack was joined to the threat
model, so importing the STRIDE worksheet pack was not enough — the browser
said "No templates found" with no hint that an unconnected pack was sitting
there. A facilitator had to connect a worksheet to their threat model as
though it described their stack.

The gate exists so that `component_ref`s resolve: the `resolved` action
turns them into component_library ids, and an AWS template inserted without
the AWS pack yields components pointing at nothing. A pack of `pack_type:
template` ships no components at all, so nothing in its templates can fail
to resolve and a connection has nothing to supply. Those are exempt; every
other pack is gated exactly as before, which the test pins in both
directions.

Found by inserting the pack against a running stack. Reading the path does
not show it — every hop from pack YAML to canvas is a passthrough, and this
sits in a queryset upstream of all of them. Confirmed by ablation: with the
clause reverted the worksheet disappears from the browser again.

fix(dfd-editor): dismiss the context menu when a cell is pressed

A selected table swallowed the pointerdown on its cells, so an open context
menu stayed open until a click landed outside the table. An unselected one
was fine, because only a selected table takes the pointer at all.

React's stopPropagation stops the native event at the root container, and
Radix dismisses layers from a pointerdown listener on document above it, so
the menu never learned the press had happened. Nothing needed the stop:
nodrag is what keeps a press from dragging the node, and no ancestor of a
cell handles pointerdown.

The same stop on the cell textarea goes with it. It cannot strand a menu —
opening one blurs the textarea and unmounts it, so the two are never open at
once — but it bought nothing either.

Three things that belong together: merging cells, the worksheet that needed
merging, and a context-menu bug the cell selection in #553 shipped with.

Select a range and merge it, so a table can carry a header spanning the columns
under it. That is what a STRIDE-per-interaction worksheet needs (#520): a
component name over its Mitigations/Weaknesses pair, which is the layout Vikram
posted and the reason this exists. That worksheet now ships as a template pack
rather than living only in my checkout.

Screenshot of the rebuilt worksheet is at `frontend/tmp/stride-merged.png` in my
checkout if you want it dropped in here; I can't attach images from the CLI.

## Behaviour, and where it comes from

Checked against the tools on 2026-09-16 rather than guessed.

**Interaction is Miro's** — select cells, *Merge cells* on the context menu, and
they can be unmerged at any time.

**Content is Excel's rule** — the anchor keeps its text, the rest are emptied.
[Microsoft](https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/excel/get-started/merge-and-unmerge-cells-in-excel):
"the contents of only one cell (the upper-left cell…) appear in the merged cell.
The contents of the other cells that you merge are deleted." Sheets is the same.

**No confirmation, unlike both of them.** They warn because in Excel and Sheets
the discarded text is gone for good — Microsoft's doc is explicit that unmerge
does not bring it back. Undo restores it here, and the table already discards
cells without asking when a row or column is removed, with the panel saying so:
*"Removing a column or row discards its cells. Undo restores them."*

**An insert or delete through a merge unmerges it.** Neither spreadsheet does
anything better. Excel expands the selection to the merge's full extent, so
inserting one row inside a ten-row merge inserts
[ten](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5033930/insert-columns-rows-where-there-are-merged-cells);
